claims.claim: A parameter is a name in a function definition, while an argument is a value supplied in a call.
Ordinary parameters can receive arguments by position or by matching keyword; positional arguments must precede keyword arguments in a call.
A default value is used when the caller does not provide that argument, and default expressions are evaluated once when the function is defined.
A parameter prefixed with * collects surplus positional arguments into a tuple.
A parameter prefixed with ** collects surplus keyword arguments into a dictionary.
Using a mutable object such as a list as a default can preserve changes between calls, so None plus initialization inside the function is a safer common pattern when a fresh list is intended.
